findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: If the 'secret' file contains a crafted string that could be interpreted as a shell command (e.g., a semicolon followed by another command)
findings.assumptions: The file 'secret' is readable and contains the password. The file path is hardcoded and not controlled by the user.

findings.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
findings.trigger: If the email body contains HTML or JavaScript code that could be executed by the recipient's email client
findings.assumptions: The email content is not sanitized before being sent. The recipients' email clients execute HTML/JS content.

findings.title: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
findings.trigger: If the password is sent in plain text over the network
findings.assumptions: The SMTP server uses TLS/SSL for encryption. If not, the password will be sent in clear text.

findings.title: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
findings.trigger: If an attacker can control the file path, they might be able to read arbitrary files on the server
findings.assumptions: The file path is hardcoded and not controlled by the user. The server has permissions to read files in the current directory.
